Vancouver-based Fidelity Investments has one of its star fund managers under investigation for stock trades made just before a remarkable sell-off in the company's shares. 
Aaron Kjelland, 40, is the manager of the Fidelity Investments Large Capitalization Real Estate team and has been with the company since 2014. The Canada-based fund manager is under scrutiny for more than 200,000 trades executed over a six-month period in the three months before April's steep sell-off, when the company's stock tanked 43 per cent.
Investigators are looking into whether Kjelland was trading ahead of client orders, the Financial Post reported, citing people familiar with the matter. 
Fidelity Investments said in a statement that it is co-operating with the enquiry. "When we have corporate compliance issues, we take swift action," Fidelity spokesperson Kendra McGregor said in an email.

One of the primary reasons why organizational structure is important for effective budgetary control is its influence on communication and decision-making processes. A well-designed organizational structure clarifies the reporting lines and establishes clear responsibilities and authorities. This enables efficient coordination and collaboration, ensuring all departments and individuals are aware of and adhere to the budgetary restrictions. For instance, a hierarchical structure may facilitate top-down communication to ensure that the budgetary control measures are uniform across the organization.
Budget planning is another critical component of achieving effective budgetary control. It involves setting goals, determining resource requirements, and developing strategies to achieve those goals. A well-constructed budget allows businesses to allocate resources strategically, identify potential areas of overspending, and take corrective actions in a timely manner. Moreover, budget planning helps organizations prioritize their investments and minimize wasteful expenses. Without proper budget planning, businesses risk overspending or allocating resources ineffectively, leading to budgetary deviations and financial instability.

Beijing Court Sentences Dissident Wang Dan to 11 Years in Prison for Plotting to Subvert Government

A Beijing Court today sentenced prominent Chinese dissident Wang Dan to 11 years in prison for “plotting to subvert the government.” Wang, 43, was a leader of the 1989 Tiananmen Square pro-democracy protests as a student. He has been in and out of prison and detention for the past 30 years for continuing his activism and criticism of the Chinese government.

Wang was secretly detained by police in August 2018 and held for over 18 months before today’s trial and sentencing. According to Wang's lawyer, the conviction was based on Wang's social media posts and communications with activists overseas that were critical of the Communist leadership. The court declared that Wang's advocacy for political change and multi-party democracy in China amounted to subversive activities that threatened national security. Human rights groups condemned the sentencing and called it unlawful retaliation against Wang for exercising his right to free speech.

Washington D.C.- Amidst increasing concerns regarding the erosion of Hong Kong's freedoms, the United States has reminded China of its responsibilities to preserve the autonomy and civil liberties of the territory post handover.
On Thursday, U.S. envoy to East Asia, Daniel Kritenbrink told reporters at a briefing, "For the United States, Hong Kong's autonomy, its freedoms, and the quality of life of its residents are of great importance and will remain so."
He went on to reaffirm Washington's support for the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration, which laid out the terms of the handover of Hong Kong from Britain to China in 1997. The agreement was designed to guarantee rights and freedoms to Hong Kong's citizens, including the right to vote, free speech, and an independent judiciary under the principle of "one country, two systems."
However, many Hong Kong citizens and international observers have grown increasingly concerned that China is steadily chipping away at Hong Kong's autonomy and freedoms.

Their value system and cultural beliefs regarding nature are significantly different. Western civilization places a high value on natural resources and, as a result, practice a land-centric conservation approach. By contrast, Native American tribes, such as the Lummi, have lived in close proximity to natural resources their entire history, and value them as part of a larger spiritual ecosystem. As a result, they practice a sky-farming conservation approach, whereby they assume stewardship of natural resources up in the sky rather than on the ground.

Despite their differences, there are also clear overlap between the value systems of the two cultures. Both Western civilization and Native American tribes recognise the intrinsic value of nature and work to preserve it as a vital part of the ecosystem upon which they depend for survival.

Incorporating both Western conservation practices and Native American tribal perspectives into decision-making processes can promote more harmonious relationships between cultures and nature.

As a result, they practice sky-based conservation, which involves stewardship of natural resources in the sky rather than on the ground. Despite their differences, there are also many similarities between the two cultures. Both Western civilization and Native American tribes recognize the intrinsic value of nature and work to preserve it as a vital part of the environment on which they depend for their existence. Including both conservation practices and the perspectives of the tribes in decision-making can promote a more harmonious relationship between people and nature.

Every day, like clockwork, my normal day consists of 25 hours instead of 24. It's something I have grown accustomed to, as though I am given an extra slice of time to spend just the way I please. Once a day, for an hour, the world stops except for me.
In this enchanted hour, I am free to explore the stillness that surrounds me. The silence is profound and soothing, as if the universe wants to give me undivided attention. Every day, I use this extraordinary hour to immerse myself in the beauty of the world that temporarily rests.
As soon as the clock strikes the designated moment, everything freezes in place. People halt mid-step, birds suspended in the air, and leaves hold their breath on the branches. It is a bizarre sight, but one that I have embraced with wonder. What used to be a fearful experience has now turned into a cherished routine.
